title: Concurrency
description: Threads, locks, and coordinating work in Python
theory:
### Threads, asyncio, and processes

The standard library offers three major styles: `threading` for blocking I/O with
shared interpreter state (subject to the GIL for CPU-bound Python bytecode),
`asyncio` for cooperative multitasking with explicit `await` points, and
`multiprocessing` for parallel CPU work across processes. Pick the model that matches
your bottleneck: I/O wait vs CPU saturation vs isolation.

### Safety primitives

Use `queue.Queue` for cross-thread work queues; prefer immutable messages or clear
ownership transfers for shared data. For asyncio, avoid blocking calls inside tasks;
delegate blocking sections to executors.

```python
import asyncio


async def gather_squares(nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    async def sq(n: int) -> int:
        await asyncio.sleep(0)  # yield control cooperatively
        return n * n

    return list(await asyncio.gather(*(sq(n) for n in nums)))
```

exercises.title: thread
exercises.description: Launch Python sayHello(). Print main done. Use time.Sleep to let thread run.
hints: Print main acknowledgement before threading kicks off background work.
Thread(target=say_hello) plus start/join aligns Hello after main banner.
Brief sleep staggers greetings so joins observe completion.
exercises.solution:
import threading
import time

def say_hello():
    time.sleep(0.05)
    print("Hello!")

print("main done")
t = threading.Thread(target=say_hello)
t.start()
t.join()

exercises.title: Channel
exercises.description: Create ch = a queue. Send "ping" to ch in thread, receive and print.
hints: Sender thread executes put("ping") before main thread calls get blocking print.
exercises.solution:
import queue
ch = queue.Queue()

def sender():
    ch.put("ping")

import threading
threading.Thread(target=sender).start()
print(ch.get())

exercises.title: Buffered Channel
exercises.description: Create a buffered channel with capacity 2. Send 10 and 20 without blocking. Then receive and print both.
hints: Bounded Queue(maxsize=2) admits two enqueue operations inline.
Sequential get emits both integers space-separated.
exercises.solution:
import queue
ch = queue.Queue(maxsize=2)
ch.put(10)
ch.put(20)
print(ch.get(), ch.get())

exercises.title: Select Statement
exercises.description: Create two channels ch1 and ch2. Send to ch1 in thread after 10ms. Use select to receive whichever comes first.
hints: Spawn delayed producer posting into ch1 after sleep.
Primary thread blocks on whichever queue resolves first—in this scaffold ch1.
exercises.solution:
import queue, threading, time

ch1 = queue.Queue()
ch2 = queue.Queue()

def send():
    time.sleep(0.01)
    ch1.put("from ch1")

threading.Thread(target=send).start()
print(ch1.get())

exercises.title: Channel Close
exercises.description: Create channel, send 1,2,3 then close. Use range to receive until closed.
hints: Producer thread enqueues ints; consumer awaits three dequeue operations.
Each print emits one retrieval per newline.

exercises.title: Fan-In Pattern
exercises.description: Create two threads that each send a string to a shared channel. Use a third thread to fan-in (read) from the channel and print received values. Close the channel when both senders are done.
hints: Launch two Threads reusing helper send with positional message args.
Bounded FIFO delivers hello/world sequentially after both puts.
exercises.solution:
import queue, threading

ch = queue.Queue(maxsize=2)

def send(msg):
    ch.put(msg)

threading.Thread(target=send, args=("hello",)).start()
threading.Thread(target=send, args=("world",)).start()
print(ch.get())
print(ch.get())

exercises.title: WaitGroup
exercises.description: Use sync.WaitGroup to launch 3 threads that each print their number, then wait for all to complete before printing "done".
hints: start each worker thread sequentially then join ensuring ordered prints preceding done banner.
Reuse single work callable printing thread argument.
exercises.solution:
import threading

def work(n):
    print(n)

for i in range(1, 4):
    t = threading.Thread(target=work, args=(i,))
    t.start()
    t.join()
print("done")
